taxonomy.subtopic: Persistent cystic-duct obstruction and gallbladder inflammation

questions.stem_html:
A 45-year-old woman develops constant right upper-quadrant pain, fever, and nausea several hours after a fatty meal. Examination shows inspiratory arrest during deep palpation below the right costal margin. Ultrasound demonstrates a stone lodged at the gallbladder neck, wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid, and a sonographic Murphy sign. The common bile duct is not dilated.

Which event most directly initiates this inflammatory process?

options.text_html: Transient obstruction of the common bile duct by a stone that has already passed
Ascending bacterial infection of a patent biliary tree as the obligatory first event
Autoimmune destruction of small intrahepatic bile ducts
Persistent obstruction of the cystic duct with gallbladder distention and mucosal ischemic injury
Pancreatic enzyme reflux through an anomalous duct junction

questions.explanation_html: Continued cystic-duct obstruction raises intraluminal pressure, stretches the gallbladder, impairs blood flow, and triggers chemical and inflammatory injury. Secondary bacterial infection may occur later. The impacted neck stone and isolated gallbladder findings localize the initiating obstruction to the cystic duct.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: A passed common-duct stone more often causes biliary colic or transient cholestasis and does not explain ongoing gallbladder inflammation.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: Bacteria can complicate cholecystitis, but persistent cystic-duct obstruction is the usual initiating event in calculous disease.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: This describes primary biliary cholangitis, not acute gallbladder inflammation.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Pancreaticobiliary reflux is not the usual mechanism of acute calculous cholecystitis.

questions.educational_objective: Differentiate acute calculous cholecystitis from biliary colic and cholangitis by identifying persistent cystic-duct obstruction, gallbladder inflammation, and characteristic ultrasound findings.
